title: Capacity Concierge — SLA banding and GPU-affinity triage for dedicated intake
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Build a lightweight intake and prioritization workflow (the 'Capacity Concierge') for enterprise Dedicated requests that standardizes SLA banding, reserved throughput sizing, and GPU-affinity decisions. This ticket scopes the customer-facing questionnaire, the internal scoring rubric, and an operational handoff checklist for infra/alloc teams. Goal: reduce triage time from 3+ days to <24 hours for requests that meet guardrails, and produce repeatable recommendations (SLA band, GPU class, burst policy) for each intake.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A one-page intake form (customer) and a one-page triage rubric (internal) exist in Confluence and have been reviewed by Eng and SRE. 2) Three SLA bands defined (Gold/Silver/Bronze) with explicit latency (P50/P95), throughput, and error budget thresholds. 3) GPU-affinity matrix mapping model classes (small/med/large/LLM-very-large) to GPU families and quantization recommendations. 4) An example of 5 historical customer requests run through the rubric with outputs recorded. 5) Handoff checklist and responsible owners (infra, networking, AM) documented.
proposal: Create a triage pipeline: (A) Customer questionnaire collects traffic patterns, token distribution, model family, latency targets, retention/PII requirements, and desired burst behavior; (B) Automated scoring rubric computes an initial SLA band and GPU-family recommendation; (C) PM/Eng review for edge cases; (D) Final recommendation produced with suggested reserved throughput, burst credits, and rollout strategy (canary vs immediate). Prototype the scoring model as a spreadsheet + simple script, then bake into the intake UI/Confluence form.
decision_log: 2025-02-14 — Decided to use three SLA bands (Gold: p95<=200ms, Silver: p95<=400ms, Bronze: p95<=800ms) instead of percentile-continuous scoring to make sales/legal conversations faster. — Attendees: Leah, Marco, Priya (SRE)

2025-02-19 — Selected GPU-affinity categories rather than per-model binding. Categories: 'embeddings/light', 'generation-small', 'generation-large', 'LLM-XL'. Each category maps to preferred GPU families and quantization guidance. Benefit: simpler runbook and fewer exceptions. — Attendees: Marco, Diego (Infra), Hana (Research)

2025-02-25 — Agreed to include burst credits concept: baseline reserved throughput + ephemeral burst pool (percentage-based) with preemption policy documented. Allowed burst up to 2x for Gold customers with 15-minute smoothing window. — Attendees: Leah, Priya, Olly (Sales)

2025-02-28 — Risk: mapping for multi-region customer with data sovereignty requirements will require Private deployment intake; route these to Private/On-prem playbook. — Attendees: Leah, Saira (Compliance)
